summary.headline: Pricol Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to Rs 1,334.02 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.82% on input cost inflation.
summary.overview: Pricol reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 1,334.02 crore, with EBITDA margin at 11.82% and PAT of Rs 85.21 crore (6.39% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 2,417.60 crore, up 29.59% YoY, with H1 EBITDA margin at 11.64%. Management said margins were hit by first-time increases in bare PCB, memory, labour and power costs, plus rupee weakness, and that pass-through to customers is under negotiation and will not be fully recovered. Growth was attributed to strong two-wheeler demand and new product launches, with all three divisions growing at roughly the same rate.

financial_highlights.change: +35.03% QoQ as stated by management (Q2 vs previous quarter); +35% YoY per Q&A
EBITDA growth 27.87% (as stated, basis not specified)

financial_highlights.value: Declined about 150 bps QoQ (analyst figure, not disputed by management)

segments.name: DICVS (driver information and clusters)
segments.commentary: Grew in line with company average of about 35% YoY in Q2; new Bajaj Pulsar launch with next-generation TFT clusters added value. Honda electronic LCD cluster business is ongoing for about two years.

segments.name: ACFMS (fuel and water pumps)
segments.commentary: Grew in line with company average of about 35% in Q2; driven by domestic two-wheeler fuel pumps and export large water pumps to US (Caterpillar cited as a large customer). Little major import content, but labour costs rose.

segments.name: Plastics (P3L)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 312 crore at 9.9% EBITDA margin. FY26 revenue was about Rs 950-1,000 crore; plant running at close to 100% capacity, with Rs 350 crore capex over the next six quarters and asset turn of about 3 to 3.25x.

guidance_outlook: Management expects input cost headwinds (bare PCBs, memory, labour, power, forex) to persist for a few more quarters before normalising.
Management hopes to conclude price pass-through negotiations with customers in Q3 FY27, but does not expect full 100% recovery.
Management estimated first-time cost escalations at 1% to 2% of EBITDA as a rough figure, while declining to give a product-level breakup or a combined margin number.
Plastics real growth expected from FY28 onwards, after capacity creation over the next 12 months.
Demerger into DICVS and ACFMS: NCLT process expected to take a couple of quarters; full operational split of the two divisions planned from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: P3L (plastics) capex of Rs 350 crore over the next six quarters, with asset turn of about 3 to 3.25x.
Plastics business operating at close to 100% capacity; next 12 months are for building new capacity before commissioning.
Internal divisionalisation of the company started from October 2026 (controls, people moved), with full operational split from 1 April 2027.
demand_pricing: Two-wheeler segment grew about 35% in Q2, against industry production growth of about 20% per the analyst; management said this was the highest two-wheeler growth in history and Pricol is heavily weighted to two-wheelers.

Pricing: quarterly index-linked pass-through for raw material and forex works as usual, but first-time increases since Q1 (bare PCB, memory chips due to AI demand, casting and machining, labour cost from new wage rules in northern India) are under negotiation with customers.
Management said market share was not lost and some was gained from new Q2 launches in DIS, plastics and ACFMS.
Plastics customers named: TVS, Ather Energy, Royal Enfield, Autoliv; Honda Motorcycles to become a key plastics customer in FY28.
Honda relationship is not new; it started about a year ago on electronic LCD clusters.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin decline (150 bps QoQ) is passed through, and what would EBITDA be without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said input costs rose from three factors (forex, bare PCBs, memory) and that EBITDA is lower than top-line growth as a result. Customer settlement is expected next quarter, but not full recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the first-time cost increases on Q2 EBITDA, and what margin would result with full pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the first-time cost escalation impact at roughly 1% to 2% of EBITDA. It declined to combine this with pass-through into a margin number, saying the impact varies by product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plastics FY26 revenue and FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 plastics revenue was close to Rs 950-1,000 crore. Management declined to give a closing-year value but said the pipeline is good and real growth starts in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the P3L Q2 revenue and EBITDA figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 P3L revenue was Rs 312 crore with EBITDA of 9.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plastics capex and asset turn?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of Rs 350 crore over the next six quarters, with asset turn of about 3 to 3.25x.

qa_highlights.question: What drove growth above industry, and was there market share gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler growth of about 35%, value-added launches such as the Bajaj TFT cluster, and US export ACFMS pumps. Management said no share was lost and some was gained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Application submitted; final NCLT orders expected in a couple of quarters. Internal divisionalisation started in October, with full split from 1 April 2027.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin pressure from bare PCB, memory, labour and power costs and rupee weakness; management expects this to last a few more quarters.
Pass-through recovery is uncertain: management does not expect full recovery, and customers may not pass costs on to end customers.
Plastics growth depends on Rs 350 crore capex being commissioned within about 12 months; current capacity is fully used.
Demerger approval from NCLT is pending and expected to take a couple of quarters.
Management did not quantify the gross-margin impact or give a clear view on Q3 margin direction; it said it was hard to predict.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and top-line growth, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins: management repeatedly declined to quantify product-level cost impact or the combined pass-through margin, and said outcomes were uncertain.
key_quotes: It could have been better. If you recall in the previous earnings call, we have explained that we continue to face very strong headwinds , primarily because of the rising input cost.
We expect these strong headwinds to continue for a few more quarters before everything gets settled down.
we expect that we would not be in a position to 100% recover from the customers, considering that everything the customer also cannot pass on to the end customer.
I cannot put A plus B is equal to C. That is why I am telling product to product it differs.

adds.what: P3L (plastics) capacity build, Rs 350 crore capex over next six quarters (asset turn ~3-3.25x)

growth.why: Q2 revenue grew ~35% YoY with two-wheeler demand and new launches, but no explicit FY guidance number was given; plastics is at ~100% utilisation with Rs 350 crore capex over six quarters (live ~4 quarters out) and real growth guided from FY28, while price pass-through is still under negotiation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 11.82% and H1 is 11.64%, with gross margin down about 150 bps QoQ; management expects input cost headwinds to persist for a few more quarters and only partial pass-through (first-time costs estimated at 1-2% of EBITDA).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Rs 350 crore P3L capex over the next six quarters is committed, with the plastics plant at close to 100% capacity and the next 12 months earmarked for building capacity before commissioning.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew about 35% YoY and H1 grew 29.59%, with two-wheeler demand running about 35% against industry growth of about 20%, and no share lost; no explicit FY volume number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rs 350 crore P3L capex is already firmly committed, with plastics utilisation near 100%, so the capex is already announced and no new announcement is needed in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no explicit FY guidance number, and margin headwinds and uncertain pass-through argue against a raise, though the top line is running about 35% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said input costs will persist for a few quarters, pass-through will not fully recover, and Q3 margin direction is hard to predict, with the gross margin down about 150 bps QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New product launches in Q2 (Bajaj Pulsar TFT clusters, DIS, plastics and ACFMS) added value, and Honda is set to become a key plastics customer in FY28; no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.label: Customer price pass-through settlement
rows.why: Management hopes to conclude first-time cost pass-through talks in Q3 FY27, but does not expect full 100% recovery on bare PCB, memory, labour and power costs.

rows.label: Demerger into DICVS and ACFMS
rows.why: NCLT process expected to take a couple of quarters, with full operational split planned from 1 April 2027 after internal divisionalisation started in October 2026.

rows.label: Honda plastics business ramp
rows.why: Honda Motorcycles is to become a key plastics customer in FY28, adding to the existing Honda electronic LCD cluster business that started about a year ago.

tone.note: Management was confident on two-wheeler demand and top-line growth of about 35% and on the Rs 350 crore plastics capex, but cautious and evasive on margins, declining to quantify product-level cost impact or a combined pass-through margin; analysts pushed on margin impact and pass-through.
